prop: This design was authored against the tetel worktree at commit b57bf8edb4c1eb59d8d86a8327179f43a9cb0829 ("design: anchor the residue at first proof, not at the last pass", 2026-08-08 17:56:46 +0200); every observation below was taken against that tree unless its own extent records otherwise.

The ticket's mechanical premise holds on this machine: the grep that `look_grep` invokes is BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD at /usr/bin/grep, it accepts both `--exclude-dir` and `--exclude` alongside the exact `-r -I -n -H -e` flag set `look_grep` already passes, `--exclude-dir='*.tetel'` prunes snapshot directories at any depth, and `--exclude='*.evidence.jsonl'` drops evidence ledgers. Nothing here was executed against GNU grep or on Linux, so the ticket's clause about "the Linux greps CI runs" is untested by this design and is asserted by no claim in it.

grep does not implement the ticket's first constraint — "an explicitly named path must still be read; only traversal skips" — and delegating that constraint to grep's flags would silently break it. Measured on BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD: a file named explicitly on the command line is skipped when `--exclude` matches it (no output, exit 1, against output and exit 0 for the identical command without the flag), and a directory named explicitly as the recursion root is skipped when `--exclude-dir` matches it (same contrast). Only one of the three cases behaves the way the constraint describes: `--exclude-dir` does not suppress a file inside an excluded directory when that file is named explicitly and searched non-recursively.

The rendered-memo exclusion the ticket sketches — "one glob for `*.tetel` directories under the search root, with the suffix stripped, passed as `--exclude`" — is unsound as written, in two independent ways measured on BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD. First, a pattern must be spelled the way grep constructs the file's name from the root as given: with a relative root, an absolute-path `--exclude` excluded nothing at all and the search returned every file, while the same path spelled relative to the root excluded exactly the intended file. Second, a suffix-stripped bare basename over-excludes: `--exclude='memo.md'` removed both a genuine rendered memo and an unrelated other/memo.md that has no sibling other/memo.md.tetel and so is not a rendered memo under the ticket's own test. The exclusion must therefore be emitted path-prefixed in the root's own spelling, never as a basename.

The exclusion disclosure can be made durable with no schema change, by writing it into the whole-search record's `label`. Two existing mechanisms carry it from there: `compose::render_facts` builds the committed memo's "Extent (captured)" column by joining extent entries' `label` fields and renders nothing else from an entry — not the `key`, not the captured output — so a label reaches every reader of the committed document; and `facts::mint` hashes each pending entry's `label` (followed by `world_root`, `world_state` and `output`) into the pin, so two searches whose exclusion sets differ pin differently even when their matched output is byte-identical.

The rendered-memo enumeration is affordable, because it is a directory-only walk while the grep it precedes must open and read every file. On the tetel worktree — 848 directories, 159,519 files, three `*.tetel` snapshot directories — enumerating the snapshot directories took 0.130s against 3.953s for a single census grep with `look_grep`'s own flags over the same root. An unreadable directory bounds the walk and the grep identically: a chmod-000 directory hiding an `x.tetel` subdirectory produced "Permission denied" from both, so the enumeration's blind spot is not larger than the grep's it feeds.

The ticket's central measurement reproduces on this tree, and the three exclusions together remove tetel's own output from a census without removing source. A census of the symbol NON_COVERAGE over the tetel worktree with `look_grep`'s flags returned 87 lines / 858,096 bytes from 15 files, of which 14 were tetel's own output — three rendered memos, three evidence ledgers, eight snapshot .jsonl files — and exactly one, src/report.rs, was source. With `--exclude-dir='*.tetel'`, `--exclude='*.evidence.jsonl'` and one path-spelled `--exclude` per stripped snapshot directory, the same census returned 2 lines / 169 bytes, from src/report.rs alone.

A change confined to `look_grep` cannot alter how an already-committed memo checks. Two exhaustive greps of the whole `src/` tree establish the isolation: `Command::new` matches in only two files, `observe.rs` (the grep inside `look_grep`, and `run_command`'s child) and `worldstate.rs` (git), so no other module spawns a process by that constructor; and `observe::` matches in only three files — `main.rs` and `mcp.rs`, which build a `LookRequest` and call `observe::dispatch` or `observe::run_command`, and `facts.rs`, where the sole occurrence is inside a doc comment. Every other file in `src/`, including every file on the check and render paths, is free of both strings and therefore neither calls into `observe` by that path nor spawns a process by that constructor.

TET-28's census requirement is currently priced by tetel's own output rather than by the symbol being censused. Measured over the tetel worktree with `look_grep`'s own flags, whole-worktree censuses of `look_grep`, `NON_COVERAGE`, `censuses`, `look_path` and `search_key` return 709,469 / 858,096 / 691,562 / 688,776 / 633,291 bytes respectively — a shared floor of roughly 0.63 MB that is present whichever symbol is sought — and dropping snapshot directories and evidence ledgers alone reduces each to between 931 and 34,595 bytes, removing 95.9% to 99.9% of what the search returned. Since `look --grep` returns its stdout to the model in full, declaring a modification target costs the author roughly two thirds of a megabyte of context per symbol, almost none of it about the symbol.

Capping what a fact stores and capping what a `look` returns are already separable in practice, and only the return path currently has any cap at all — imposed downstream, not by tetel. Taking this design's one census, `look --grep look_grep` rooted at the tetel worktree, the search succeeded and was recorded, but the agent harness refused to return the result, reporting 707,751 characters across 38 lines as exceeding its maximum allowed tokens and spilling it to a file; the author therefore never read the output of their own census, while the full captured output was nonetheless minted into the fact and ships in the snapshot. The census's own extent shows why: of the ten files matched, eight are tetel's own output — three snapshot `facts.jsonl`, one snapshot `claims.jsonl`, one snapshot `prose.jsonl`, two evidence ledgers and one rendered memo — and two, `src/observe.rs` and `src/worldstate.rs`, are source.

The explicit-path exception must be implemented as a decision about whether to pass exclusion flags at all, and `look_grep`'s existing shape already supplies the discriminator. `look_grep` adds `-r` only when `root_path.is_dir()`, and passes `root` through to grep verbatim as the caller spelled it, never canonicalized. So the rule is: when the root is not a directory the caller has named a single file explicitly, and no exclusion flag is passed — which is required, since `--exclude` otherwise suppresses a file named on the command line. When the root is a directory that is itself tetel content, again no exclusion flag is passed — which is required, since `--exclude-dir` otherwise suppresses a directory named as the recursion root. Only in the remaining case, a directory root that is not itself tetel content, are the three exclusions passed, and each must be spelled the way grep will construct the matched file's name from that same root string.

TET-28's census requirement is currently priced by tetel's own output rather than by the symbol being censused. Measured over the tetel worktree with `look_grep`'s own flags, whole-worktree censuses of `look_grep`, `NON_COVERAGE`, `censuses`, `look_path` and `search_key` return 709,469 / 858,096 / 691,562 / 688,776 / 633,291 bytes respectively — a shared floor of roughly 0.63 MB that is present whichever symbol is sought — and dropping snapshot directories and evidence ledgers alone reduces each to between 931 and 34,595 bytes, removing 95.9% to 99.9% of what the search returned. Those are bytes the search returns from grep and bytes the fact then stores; how many of them reach any particular caller's context is a separate quantity this claim does not assert.
why: F10 and F12 together refute the final clause as I wrote it. C9 asserted that the census cost "is paid in the author's context", inferring context consumption from the fact that look_grep returns its stdout uncapped. F10 records that when this design took exactly such a census, the client harness rejected the 707,751-character result and returned about 1,300 characters instead — so the bytes look_grep returns and the bytes that reach a model's context are not the same quantity, and the second does not follow from the first. F12 pins what is actually true of tetel: the return is uncapped in observe.rs, which is a property of tetel, while the truncation is a property of one caller. The claim is narrowed to the two quantities that were measured — what the search returns and what the fact stores — and the context inference is removed.

prop: The ticket's headline reframing — that census output cost "~135k tokens, roughly 40% of the designer's reported 336k run" — is not reproducible from this design's evidence, and this run produced a direct counter-instance rather than merely failing to confirm it. `look_grep`'s return is genuinely uncapped in tetel: `printed.push_str(&stdout)` copies the grep's whole stdout into what `LookOutcome` hands back, with no length check, truncation or configuration between them. But when this design took a real whole-worktree census, the client harness rejected the 707,751-character result and returned roughly 1,300 characters of error text naming a spill file instead. So a large census's bytes need not enter a model's context at all, and the uncapped return does not by itself establish any figure in tokens. What the uncapped return does establish is narrower and still worth fixing: the bound that fired belongs to the caller, not to tetel, and a different caller will not supply one.

`check`'s standing non-coverage list needs a second line rather than an amendment to the one it has. The existing entry reads "whatever the platform's grep skipped — symlinked directories and binary files bound what a whole-worktree search physically visited": both causes it names are platform accidents, and nothing in it contemplates something tetel itself declined to visit. The list's own census block explains its purpose as saying what a census "cannot see", "because a refusal that fired is easily read as coverage it never claimed" — which is exactly the reason a deliberate exclusion must appear, and exactly the reason it must not be folded into the accident line. Every entry is a static string and none is per-search, so the standing line can only say that the policy exists; what a given search actually excluded is not something this list can carry.

TET-28's census predicate needs no change, and this is what makes the two disclosures divide cleanly. `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads exactly five things — that the kind is `Search` or `NoMatch`, that the pattern byte-equals the symbol, that `world_root` is non-empty and not `NO_GIT`, and that `key == world_root` — and never reads `label` or `output`. A worktree-rooted search therefore still censuses after this change, correctly, because the predicate was always about a search's existence and rooting rather than about what it found. What changes is not the predicate but what a passing census entitles a reader to conclude, and that is carried by text: a standing line in `check` saying the exclusion policy exists, and the search record's own `label` saying which patterns this particular search was given.

"No `look` returns tetel's own content" is not the honest name for what this design builds, and the honest name is better rather than merely narrower: a `look` returns tetel's own output only when the caller named it. `look_path` refuses a directory and reads exactly the one file it was given, with no traversal of any kind, so every file it can ever return is one the caller named explicitly and it is left unchanged by this design. `look_grep` is where the whole mechanism lands, and its rule is the same sentence applied to a search — the exclusions are passed only when the root is a directory that is not itself tetel content, so what they remove is only ever reached by traversal. Stating the guarantee over naming rather than over `look`'s two modes covers both with one sentence and does not promise a reader something `look_path` never did.

No opt-out flag should be added, because three escape hatches already exist and each is reached by naming something rather than by setting a flag. `look_path` opens any single named file, including one inside a snapshot, and is untouched by this design. `look --grep` rooted at a path that is itself tetel content passes no exclusions at all, which is not merely permitted but forced: grep's `--exclude-dir` suppresses a directory named as the recursion root, so the flags must be withheld there or naming a snapshot directory would return nothing. And `run` spawns `argv` directly with nothing between the empty-argv refusal and the spawn that inspects, parses or classifies the command or the paths it will touch, so it has no place a path exclusion could be applied even in principle. A flag would add a fourth route that, unlike all three of these, leaves no trace in what was named.

The pin's non-stationarity is relocated rather than removed, and the relocation is the improvement. Measured on a scratch tree: rendering a second memo into it, changing no source, left the matched output of a search for the same symbol byte-identical while changing the emitted exclusion list from one rendered-memo pattern to two. So the captured output is now stationary against tetel's own churn — which was the ticket's within-run complaint, since an evidence ledger growing during grading no longer reaches the search at all — but the exclusion set is not, and because the design writes that set into the search record's label and the label is inside the pin, two censuses of the same symbol against the same source will still pin differently across a render. The difference is that the cause is now written in plain text in the same record, instead of being an invisible change in what the search happened to read.

A directory containing nothing but tetel's output is still not "explicitly named", and the cost of that is concrete rather than theoretical. `docs/design` holds exactly nine entries — three rendered memos, three evidence ledgers, three snapshot directories — and nothing else. A search rooted there for the symbol `census` returns 184 lines and 1,200,881 bytes today; under this rule it returns nothing and exits 1. The alternative, treating a directory as named when everything beneath it happens to be tetel's, is a judgement about a directory's contents rather than a test on a path, and the project rules that out as a refusal trigger. So the exclusion stays a format test on the root itself, and the price is that searching across memos requires naming a memo file or a snapshot directory rather than the folder they sit in.

The explicit-path exception must be implemented as a decision about whether to pass exclusion flags at all, and `look_grep`'s existing shape already supplies the discriminator. `look_grep` adds `-r` only when `root_path.is_dir()`, and passes `root` through to grep verbatim as the caller spelled it, never canonicalized. So the rule is: when the root is not a directory the caller has named a single file explicitly, and no exclusion flag is passed — which is required, since `--exclude` otherwise suppresses a file named on the command line. When the root is a directory that is itself tetel content, again no exclusion flag is passed — which is required, since `--exclude-dir` otherwise suppresses a directory named as the recursion root. A root counts as tetel content by three format tests and no others: some component of it ends with the literal `.tetel`, or its filename ends with `.evidence.jsonl`, or a directory named by appending `.tetel` to it exists. Only in the remaining case, a directory root that is not itself tetel content, are the three exclusions passed, and each must be spelled the way grep will construct the matched file's name from that same root string.
why: Writing P19 and P27 exposed that C11 used the phrase "a directory that is itself tetel content" without saying what decides it, which leaves the memo's central rule resting on an undefined term — exactly the place the project requires a format test rather than a judgement. The three tests are the same three the ticket proposes for the artifacts, applied to the root instead of to a traversed file, so stating them costs nothing new and closes the gap.

Symlinked directories and any other traversal difference between the two walks were never compared. Narrowed to the mode that was actually measured.

why: P18 asserts that the truncation left no trace in the fact's extent, and no claim carried it — the exact defect the editorial check exists to catch. F12 does establish it: nothing in look_grep records that anything downstream bounded what it returned. Adding the clause to C12 rather than cutting the sentence, because it is the observation that makes the ticket's own second constraint bite against the client rather than against tetel.

prop: A change confined to `look_grep` cannot alter how an already-committed memo checks, for two independent reasons. The first is call-graph isolation: two exhaustive greps of the whole `src/` tree show `Command::new` matching in only `observe.rs` (the grep inside `look_grep`, and `run_command`'s child) and `worldstate.rs` (git), and `observe::` matching in only `main.rs` and `mcp.rs`, which build a `LookRequest` and dispatch it, and `facts.rs`, where the sole occurrence is inside a doc comment — so every other file in `src/`, including every file on the check and render paths, neither calls into `observe` by that path nor spawns a process by that constructor. The second is immutability: the `tetel fact` module doc states that a revision rewrites the note only, and that "extent, output and pin are set once at mint time and never appear in a revision event at all, so there is no code path that could change them later either". A fact minted under the old behaviour therefore keeps the extent and pin it was minted with, whatever a later `look` would now do.
why: P31 closed on the immutability of the three committed memos' extents and pins, and C8 as written carried only the call-graph isolation, leaving that sentence resting on nothing — the defect the editorial pass exists to catch. F18 supplies it from the `tetel fact` module doc, which states that extent, output and pin never appear in a revision event at all. Folding it in makes the claim answer the whole question rather than half of it.

prop: The invariance of the three committed memos was demonstrated rather than only argued, against the one input the proposed mechanism actually depends on. `tetel check` was run over tet28's, tet29's and tet30's memos while docs/design held three snapshot directories, and again after this memo was rendered there, making four — a change in exactly the set of tetel artifacts from which the exclusion set would be computed. All three memos produced byte-identical output across the two runs: the same exit code, the same byte count, and the same SHA-256 of combined stdout and stderr (3cdf677b… / 5097feb5… / b3bca4fd…).

This design was authored against the tetel worktree at commit b57bf8edb4c1eb59d8d86a8327179f43a9cb0829 ("design: anchor the residue at first proof, not at the last pass", 2026-08-08 17:56:46 +0200), and no tracked source file differs from that commit. Which tree each individual observation was taken against is not asserted here: every observation records its own working-tree marker, and `check` reports those states directly.
why: Grounding pass k1 qualified C1: the pin clause is exact and the tree unmodified, but the second clause — "every observation below was taken against that tree unless its own extent records otherwise" — is a statement about the author's own capture history that no pass working from source alone can settle. It was also unnecessary, because each observation's working-tree marker is recorded by the tool per entry and check reports the states this memo's facts were taken against. Narrowed to the two things a grounder can and did check.

prop: The explicit-path exception must be implemented as a decision about whether to pass exclusion flags at all, and `look_grep`'s existing shape already supplies the discriminator. `look_grep` adds `-r` only when `root_path.is_dir()`, and passes `root` through to grep verbatim as the caller spelled it, never canonicalized. So the rule is: when the root is not a directory the caller has named a single file explicitly, and no exclusion flag is passed — which is required, since `--exclude` otherwise suppresses a file named on the command line. When the root is a directory with a path component ending in the literal `.tetel`, again no exclusion flag is passed — which is required, since `--exclude-dir` otherwise suppresses a directory named as the recursion root. That single component test is the whole of the root predicate: the other two artifacts, an evidence ledger and a rendered memo, are files rather than directories, so a root naming either takes the not-a-directory branch and never reaches a content test at all. Only in the remaining case, a directory root with no `.tetel` component, are the three exclusions passed, and each must be spelled the way grep will construct the matched file's name from that same root string.
why: Grounding pass k1 flagged a wording seam it declined to refute: the third format test — appending `.tetel` and checking the directory exists — can only ever fire for a *file* root, while the sentence around it speaks of a directory root. Working it through, the seam is a redundancy rather than a phrasing problem. The other two artifacts, an evidence ledger and a rendered memo, are files, so a root naming either already takes the not-a-directory branch and never reaches the content test at all. Only a `.tetel` path component can decide a directory root. Reduced to the one test that can fire, which is both simpler and the thing an implementer would otherwise get subtly wrong.
